MY LITTLE SCIENCE PROJECT

How to Grow a Bean

Set up a tiny science project with a grown-up. Make a prediction, then check your bean each day.

Soak untreated planting beans overnight. Dampen a paper towel, tuck it inside an open clear cup, and put the beans between the towel and cup wall. Keep the cup warm in indirect daylight. Keep the towel damp, not soaking. Once roots and leaves develop, ask an adult to help move the seedling into soil.

With a grown-up: use untreated planting beans; do not eat seeds or sprouts. Keep small seeds away from younger children. Wash hands after handling. An adult should discard any mouldy setup.

LOOK · THINK · TRY

Explore before you start.

Seeds need water, air and a suitable temperature to germinate. Their stored food supports early growth. The leaves later use light to help the plant make food.

Look at the picture, talk about what you notice, then use the drawing and writing spaces below. Open the picture for a closer look.

Why a clear cup?

The cup lets you watch roots appear without digging up the seed. Turn it gently to look from different sides.

Damp, not flooded

Squeeze excess water from the towel before placing it in the cup. Seeds need air as well as water; a pool at the bottom is not the goal.

What should I look for?

Notice changes in the seed coat, a small root and then a shoot. Record the order you observe rather than expecting a fixed timetable.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.
